localities.name: County Cork
localities.blurb: Ireland's largest county. Civil registration starts in 1864, so Catholic parish registers carry most family lines before that, and much of the 19th-century census was destroyed.
events: Non-Catholic marriages first registered
Civil registration of all births, marriages and deaths begins
Public Record Office fire destroys most 19th-century census returns and many wills

localities.name: New York City
localities.blurb: Five boroughs joined in 1898. Before then Brooklyn kept its own registers, and the port added its own trail of arrival records.
events: Castle Garden opens as the state immigrant landing depot
Metropolitan Board of Health begins systematic vital registration
Ellis Island opens
Brooklyn, Queens and Staten Island join Manhattan and the Bronx as one city
Fire damages the 1890 federal census

localities.name: Suffolk
localities.blurb: Parish and civil records sit mostly with Suffolk Archives, which has three branches. Civil registration for England and Wales begins in 1837.
events: Parish registers ordered to be kept
Hardwicke's Marriage Act requires church weddings
Civil registration begins in England and Wales
Civil courts take over probate
repos: Ipswich, Bury St Edmunds and Lowestoft branches

localities.name: Palermo
localities.blurb: Sicilian civil registers start in 1820 under the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies. The unified Italian system follows from 1866, and parish books reach back much further.
events: Civil registers begin in the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies
Sicily joins the Kingdom of Italy
The Italian civil register system takes over

localities.name: Kraków
localities.blurb: The city passed from the Free City period to Austrian Galicia and then back to Poland, so records sit with Austrian, church and Polish authorities.
events: Free City of Kraków created
Austria annexes the city
Poland regains independence

localities.name: Jalisco
localities.blurb: Catholic registers reach back to the 1500s and are largely digitized. Civil registration begins in the 1860s, and notarial and government papers are in Guadalajara.
events: Civil registration law passed in Mexico
The Revolution begins and some local records are disrupted
repos: Archivo de Instrumentos Públicos de Jalisco
Archivo Histórico del Arzobispado de Guadalajara

localities.name: Québec
localities.blurb: Parish registers are unusually complete from 1621, kept in duplicate with a civil copy. A civil registrar replaced them as the official record in 1994.
events: Earliest surviving parish register
Treaty of Paris cedes New France to Britain
Civil registrar replaces parish registers as the official record
repos: Archives centres in Montréal, Québec City and the regions

localities.name: Jefferson County
localities.blurb: Louisville is the county seat. Statewide birth and death registration begins in 1911, county clerks hold marriages and deeds, and two early census years are lost.
events: Jefferson County created within Virginia
Kentucky becomes a state
Statewide birth and death registration begins
repos: Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives
University of Louisville Archives and Special Collections

records.title: Civil registration of births
records.notes: Indexes and register images. The end year moves forward as older records pass the privacy threshold, so check the site for the current limit.

records.title: Civil registration of marriages
records.notes: Non-Catholic marriages are registered from 1845 and all marriages from 1864.

records.title: Civil registration of deaths
records.notes: Check the site for the latest year released.

records.title: Catholic parish registers
records.notes: Free page images. Start dates vary by parish and many Cork parishes begin in the early 1800s. The registers are not indexed by name, so search by parish.

records.title: Tithe Applotment Books
records.notes: Lists occupiers of agricultural land and the tithe due. Landless people do not appear.

records.title: Griffith's Valuation
records.notes: Lists occupiers and landlords by townland. Cork was surveyed in the early 1850s.

records.title: Census of Ireland, 1901 and 1911
records.notes: Full household returns. Returns for 1821 to 1851 were largely destroyed in 1922, and those for 1861 to 1891 were destroyed by the government.

records.title: Calendars of wills and administrations
records.notes: Indexed by surname, with the district registry noted.

records.title: Local government and poor law records
records.notes: Council, poor law union and private collections. Ask for finding aids before you visit.

records.title: Birth certificates and index
records.notes: Online index. Certificate copies are ordered from the Municipal Archives. Earlier Manhattan records are patchy.

records.title: Marriage certificates and index
records.notes: Search the index by groom or bride, note the borough, then request the certificate.

records.title: Death certificates and index
records.notes: Index online, copies by request.

records.title: US federal census
records.notes: Most of the 1890 schedules burned in 1921. The 1950 census is free to search at the National Archives.

records.title: New York State census
records.notes: Taken in 1825, 1835 and so on to 1875, then in 1892, 1905, 1915 and 1925. Coverage of the city varies by year.

records.title: Ellis Island passenger records
records.notes: Free with registration. Manifests list age, last residence and a contact at the destination.

records.title: New York passenger lists
records.notes: Index and images of arrivals at the port, including the Castle Garden years from 1855 to 1890.

records.title: 1940 tax photographs
records.notes: A photograph of every building in the five boroughs, searchable by address.

records.title: Brooklyn Daily Eagle
records.notes: Searchable through the library. Check the library for current access terms.

records.title: Old Fulton NY Post Cards
records.notes: A large free archive of New York newspapers. Coverage differs by title and search results can be noisy.

records.title: WWI draft registration cards
records.notes: Men aged 18 to 45, including many recent immigrants. Cards give birth date, employer and nearest relative.

records.title: Surrogate's Court wills and probate
records.notes: Wills and probate files for New York counties. Each borough has its own Surrogate's Court, so check the county first.

records.title: Civil registration index (FreeBMD)
records.notes: Index only, for England and Wales. Order certificates from the General Register Office. Coverage thins in later years.

records.title: Parish registers, originals and microfilm
records.notes: Held at the Ipswich, Bury St Edmunds and Lowestoft branches. Registers were ordered kept from 1538.

records.title: Parish register transcriptions (FreeREG)
records.notes: Volunteer transcriptions. Coverage of Suffolk parishes is uneven, so confirm against the original where you can.

records.title: Census of England and Wales
records.notes: Household returns. The 1921 census is held by Findmypast, and some years have free indexes on FamilySearch.

records.title: 1939 Register
records.notes: Wartime household listing. Entries for people who may still be living are closed or redacted.

records.title: Tithe maps and apportionments
records.notes: Maps and lists of landowners and occupiers by parish. Duplicates are at The National Archives.

records.title: Prerogative Court of Canterbury wills
records.notes: Wills of wealthier testators. The catalogue is online, and download terms are listed at the Archives.

records.title: National probate calendar
records.notes: Annual index of grants of probate in England and Wales. Copies of wills can be ordered.

records.title: Ipswich Journal
records.notes: Regional newspaper covering much of Suffolk. Check the title list for gaps in the run.

records.title: Stato civile (civil registration)
records.notes: Images of civil registers held by the Archivio di Stato di Palermo. The span varies by comune and name indexes are partial.

records.title: Parish and diocesan registers
records.notes: Start dates vary by parish, and many begin in the decades after the Council of Trent. Write ahead to arrange access.

records.title: Notarial deeds
records.notes: Contracts, dowries, wills and property sales, arranged by notary. Useful before civil registration begins.

records.title: Conscription lists (liste di leva)
records.notes: Men listed by birth year. Digitization differs by archive, so check Palermo's holdings.

records.title: Parish record index (Geneteka)
records.notes: Volunteer index that points to the parish, year and act number. Images are held elsewhere.

records.title: Digitized parish registers
records.notes: Page images from the Polish State Archives. Not every parish is digitized. Entries are in Latin, Polish or German depending on the period.

records.title: Jewish records index (JRI-Poland)
records.notes: Index of Jewish vital records. Search the index, then find the image through the archive.

records.title: City, court and family papers
records.notes: Contact the archive in advance. Finding aids are partly online.

records.title: Małopolska Digital Library
records.notes: Free newspapers, directories and books from southern Poland, mostly in Polish.

records.title: Catholic parish and diocesan registers
records.notes: Images of baptisms, marriages and burials. Browse by municipality and parish. Name indexing is partial.

records.title: Civil registration (Registro Civil)
records.notes: Mexico began civil registration in 1859. Jalisco entries start in the 1860s and vary by municipality.

records.title: Notarial and property records
records.holder: Archivo de Instrumentos Públicos de Jalisco
records.notes: Notarial protocols and property deeds for Guadalajara and the state. Ask the archive about finding aids.

records.title: Colonial and state government records
records.notes: Court, municipal and government papers. Often the only source for land disputes and local office holders.

records.title: Mexican border crossing records
records.notes: Arrivals at U.S. land ports from Mexico. Useful for tracing a relative who moved north.

records.title: Catholic parish registers
records.notes: Images of the registers, with duplicate civil copies for many years. Name indexing varies by period.

records.title: Drouin Collection
records.notes: Indexed registers for Québec, with some Ontario and New England parishes.

records.title: Early Québec population register (PRDH)
records.notes: Reconstructed individual and family records for the French and early British regimes. Check current access terms.

records.title: Notarial records
records.notes: Contracts, marriage settlements and inventories. Many are digitized and the rest are consulted at BAnQ centres.

records.title: Census of Canada
records.notes: Household returns with digitized pages. The 1931 census opened in 2023, 92 years after it was taken. Not every year survives for every district.

records.title: First World War personnel files
records.notes: Digitized service files of the Canadian Expeditionary Force. Search by name or regimental number.

records.title: Kentucky death certificates
records.notes: Statewide registration begins in 1911. Compliance is uneven in the first few years.

records.title: Early county birth registers
records.holder: Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives
records.notes: County-level registers survive for some years in the 1850s and 1870s and coverage is patchy. Statewide birth certificates begin in 1911.

records.title: Kentucky county marriages index
records.notes: Index of county marriage records. Jefferson County was formed in 1780 as part of Virginia. Originals are with the county clerk.

records.title: US federal census
records.notes: The 1790 and 1800 Kentucky schedules are lost. Tax lists from the 1790s stand in for them.

records.title: Louisville city directories
records.notes: Scanned directories list heads of household with occupation and address. Coverage differs by year.

records.title: Manuscript and family collections
records.notes: Family papers, church records and photographs for the Louisville area. Contact the library for finding aids and hours.

records.title: Deed books
records.notes: Property deeds and mortgages. Ask the clerk's office which volumes are open to the public.
